cards.explanation: The answer is that life is more than food. Jesus says, “For life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.” Food and clothes matter, friends, but they aren't the whole story of a life. So when the what-will-I-wear and what-will-I-eat list starts spinning, this line is worth grabbing.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “They do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn; yet God feeds them.” That little word “yet” carries the whole point, friends. No barn, and the ravens are still fed.

The word is valuable. Jesus says, “How much more valuable you are than the birds!” He points at birds God already feeds, then says the disciples are worth far more. When you feel small, friends, hold onto that word.

The answer is True. Jesus asks, “Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?” Then He says, “So if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest?” An hour is the small thing, friends, and worry can't even do that.

The answer is that Jesus asks why they worry about the rest. He says, “So if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest?” If worry can't buy one hour, bakers, it isn't going to handle the big stuff either. He's pointing out that worry hasn't done the job.

The answer is Solomon. Solomon was David's son and Israel's king (1 Kings 2:12). Jesus says, “…not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.” A king in his glory, friends, outdressed by a flower.

The answer is that God will clothe them much more. Jesus says, “If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more will He clothe you…” Grass that's gone tomorrow still gets clothed, bakers, so the disciples can count on far more. No condition attached.
The answer is False. Jesus says God will clothe them much more, and then adds, “…O you of little faith!” No praise for great faith here, friends. It's a gentle nudge to trust more.

The answer is that the Father knows they need them. Jesus says, “…your Father knows that you need them.” The Gentiles strive after all these things, but the disciples have a Father who already knows what they need. Nobody has to nag Him about it, friends.
The answer is their Father's kingdom. Jesus says, “But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.” The kingdom is the thing to chase, friends. The rest gets added.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.” The "things" are what He's been talking about, friends: food, drink and clothes. He tells them to seek the kingdom, and He says these things will be added.
The word is pleased. Jesus says, “Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.” The Father is pleased to give it, bakers. It isn't a grudging handout.
The answer is in heaven. Jesus says, “…an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.” That purse will not wear out, friends. And in heaven, no thief approaches.

The answer is False. Jesus describes the treasure as “…an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.” The moth is on the list of things that don't destroy it, friends. Jesus says no thief approaches it either.

The answer is your heart. Jesus says, “For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.” Your heart will be right where your treasure is, friends. So it's worth asking where yours is parked.
